reason: Gravitational focusing can help rocky planetesimals gather into larger bodies.
expectation: The planetesimals will grow into a rocky embryo or a precursor to one.

effect: Crossing orbits, rather than gravitational focusing directly, produced accreting embryos; I can now try adding volatile-bearing material.
reaction: The automatic combination was a useful correction to my initial guess.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock could supply volatiles to the growing embryos.
expectation: The embryos will incorporate hydrated rock toward a volatile-bearing young Earth.

effect: The embryos cannot yet incorporate the water-bearing rock; their available partners are gravitational focusing and rocky planetesimals.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarifies that further growth comes first.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the accreting embryos grow by attracting more material.
expectation: The embryos will grow into larger planetary bodies.

alternatives.reason: Adding more planetesimals is another listed route for growth.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced a strongly attracting embryo, which may now gather water-bearing rock.
reaction: The growth mechanism is clearer now.
reason: The larger embryo is a plausible body to accrete hydrated asteroid material.
expectation: The embryo will incorporate volatile-bearing material toward becoming a young Earth.

effect: The embryo first needed rocky fragments to become a proto-Earth; I can now try adding the hydrated rock.
reaction: The automatic correction clarified the sequence.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock is the visible source of volatiles for the rocky proto-Earth.
expectation: The proto-Earth will incorporate hydrated material and become volatile-bearing.

effect: The rocky proto-Earth currently has no available combinations, so adding hydrated rock is not yet possible through it.
reaction: The repeated delay is a little frustrating, but the other known growth route remains.
reason: Rocky planetesimals are a previously listed partner for the accreting embryos and may advance the other embryo goal.
expectation: The embryos will gather more rocky material, potentially producing another rocky embryo.

reaction: Theia's uncertain identity makes the second embryo more interesting.
reason: The proto-Earth had no available operation, so inspecting the hydrated rock may reveal another way to incorporate volatiles.

expectation: The inspection will reveal a compatible partner, and automatically combine it if there is only one operation.

effect: The collision exposed asteroid core fragments, which may provide the missing ingredient for the proto-Earth.
reaction: Exposing metal from a differentiated body is an interesting connection to iron meteorites.
reason: The newly exposed core fragments may be the next material needed by the rocky proto-Earth.
expectation: The proto-Earth will incorporate the metal-rich fragments, potentially opening the route to adding hydrated rock.

effect: The proto-Earth incorporated metal-rich fragments; it may now be ready to accrete hydrated rock.
reaction: The distinction between inherited metal and Earth's later differentiation is useful.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock is the remaining visible source of volatiles for the growing Earth.
expectation: The proto-Earth will incorporate hydrated material and become volatile-bearing.

effect: The hydrated rock completed the volatile-bearing young Earth and the chapter; other sources and the timing of its water remain uncertain.
reaction: It was satisfying to finally incorporate the hydrated material after the earlier dead ends.

mostWorthwhile.text: Exposing and incorporating asteroid core fragments connected differentiation in smaller bodies to Earth's inherited material, with a useful link to iron meteorites.

leastWorthwhile.text: Repeated attempts to add hydrated rock before the required intermediate steps were frustrating, particularly when the proto-Earth had no available combinations.

surprise.text: The proto-Earth needed metal from an already differentiated asteroid before it could take in the water-bearing rock.

arbitrary.text: That ordering felt somewhat arbitrary: the results explained what each accretion event contributed, but not why the hydrated rock had to wait until after the metal.

continue.text: I would continue: the connections between asteroid interiors, planetary growth and uncertain water sources make me curious about what happens next, despite the frustrating bottleneck.
